svg.title: Two labs, two routes into life sciences (October 20, 2026)
svg.desc: Two columns. Left, Anthropic: a research demonstration published October 20 in which an internal Claude research model, working mainly autonomously under supervision with four follow-up prompts over about 64 hours, ran a protein-design campaign for antivenom research; 211 candidates were tested by two outside contract labs and 17 met the binding criteria, about 8 percent; all designs and binding data were released publicly; Anthropic states the work is early-stage and not a treatment. Right, OpenAI: an acquisition announced October 20 of Orchestra Bio, a San Francisco start-up founded in 2022 with about 20 million dollars raised, whose agents handle drug-development operations such as study monitoring, finance tracking and clinical-trial scheduling; the team joins OpenAI's Rosalind life-sciences unit and the price was not disclosed. A bottom strip notes the contrast: Anthropic is publishing results from its own models doing science, while OpenAI is buying the workflow layer around trials; neither has shown a clinical outcome.
